Two threads: the edge case 1 explanation you asked for, and your new confirm-step idea as interrogate round 3.

## Edge case 1, explained

The state: two projects are registered, every project agent is stopped, so per the approved rule every project pod hides. Meanwhile the coordinator (and maybe a home agent like plan-review-1) is live and working.

What the captured code does in that state: it falls into the branch that a home with NO registered projects uses (decision 10 of tui-v2). That branch was written for a home where there is truly nothing else to show, so it draws only the notice and nothing else:

  What the code draws today in this state:

  ┌─ project agents · 0 projects · h shows 3 stopped ─┐
  │  no project agents                                │
  │                                                   │
  │      (no coordinator card, no home pod)           │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   [graph] ←→ select pod · ↑ coordinator · enter open pod

  Two wrong things: a live coordinator is invisible, and the footer still names it and pod navigation.

The choice is only about this all-hidden state:

  Choice A (REC): notice + live home cards

  ┌─ project agents · 0 projects · h shows 3 stopped ─┐
  │  no project agents                                │
  │  ╭──────────────────────╮                         │
  │  │ ● coordinator-g12    │                         │
  │  └──────────────────────┘                         │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

With A, the notice alone shows only when nothing at all is visible, and the no-registered-project case (decision 10) stays as it is. A live agent can then never leave the screen.

Answer it on ask card a6.

## Your confirm step: interrogate round 3

**How it works today.** In an ask card you pick with arrows, space, 1..5, or a click, tab adds a note, and enter on the last question sends the card at once. There is no look-before-send. The a1 card today showed the cost: the card sent, you said "stop that was not right", and the fix cost a re-ask (a2).

**What we need to decide.** Whether enter on the last question first opens a review of all picks, and when.

**The review view (proposed).** Enter on the last question opens a confirm state in the same card:

  ╭─ ? coordinator asks · confirm ──────────────╮
  │ g1 close    → Close both                    │
  │ dev-main PR → Open now                      │
  │ Manager     → pi + DeepSeek                 │
  │                                             │
  │ enter send · ↑↓ question to change · x drop │
  ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────╯

enter there sends. ↑↓ highlights a question, enter on it goes back to that question to change the pick or the note. x and J/K keep their meanings.

| Choice | Answer | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (REC) | Review on every card | One rule: the send enter always first shows the review. Notes and multi-picks visible at send time | Every answer costs one extra enter |
| B | Review only on cards with 2+ questions | One-question cards keep one-enter send | The send enter behaves differently by card shape |
| C | No review, as today | No change | The a1 mistake path stays |

Answer on ask card a7.

Settled, I read your two A answers in order:
1. Edge case 1: A. In the all-hidden state, the screen shows the "no project agents" notice plus the home pod with its live cards. A live agent can never leave the screen.
2. Confirm step: A. Every ask card gets the review step before send.

I sent all three decisions to manager-hive: the worker updates the six scenario grids, installs the golden files, verifies, and lands task 134 under g9. (The open cards a6 and a7 are now moot; answer or dismiss them with x as you like.)

## Confirm step: plan summary, please confirm

Decisions so far: review on every card (your 2A), and the review view as proposed in c185: enter on the last question opens the review; enter there sends; ↑↓ highlights a question and enter on it goes back to change the pick or note; x and J/K keep their meanings.

The plan:
1. Goal g10-ask-confirm on hive, one wave, grant: your answer to ask a5 (grids + child pod) and this confirm.
2. The change on the ask card: the review state before send, with the keys above. The answer prompt format does not change.
3. In the review, picks and notes show in full. Only ↑↓, enter, x, and J/K act there; 1..5 does not change a pick inside the review.
4. The task brings code grids for your approval before golden files change, like tasks 126, 131, and 134.
5. Acceptance: tests fail when enter sends without the review, and pass with it; then a live check in the real TUI.
6. manager-hive runs it after task 134 lands, on codex + gpt-6.1-sol.

| Choice | Answer |
|---|---|
| A (REC) | Confirmed: create the goal and send it to manager-hive |
| B | Correct something: tell me the number |

Confirmed. Goal g10-ask-confirm is open (wave A, done when it lands on dev) and manager-hive has it with the full review-state rules. It runs after task 134 lands, on codex + gpt-6.1-sol. Code grids come to you for approval before golden files change, and I tell you when each task lands.
